headline: Lionel Messi bids emotional farewell to Argentina in final international match
summary: Tributes from teammates like Neymar and Rodrigo De Paul, along with tearful fans, marked the historic occasion as the football icon played his 208th and final game for his country.
details: Tributes poured in for Argentine great Lionel Messi on Tuesday as the country prepared to bid farewell to their captain in his final international appearance. Former and current teammates, alongside tearful fans outside the Monumental stadium, honored the football legend.

Brazil's Neymar, Messi's former Barcelona and Paris St Germain teammate, expressed gratitude for Messi's contributions to the sport. He stated, "It's not only Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you have done for football."

Rodrigo De Paul, Messi's close friend and Argentina teammate, highlighted Messi's impact beyond football. He shared, "He made me grow not only as a footballer, but also as a person. I became a better person, a better human being, a better athlete, a better father and a better friend."

Former Argentina teammate Angel Di Maria acknowledged the bittersweet nature of the day. He remarked, "Seeing him with so much happiness, and that tranquillity of knowing that he gave everything he had, is what makes us all happy."
In Buenos Aires, fans flocked to the Monumental stadium for the Argentina vs. Benin friendly, expressing a mix of gratitude and sadness. Many shared emotional goodbyes to their national hero.

Nineteen-year-old Jose Garracedo told Reuters TV, "I cried because I was able to come and see Messi in his last game, and also because of the sadness of knowing that he won't be here anymore." He praised Messi's dedication to the shirt.

Medical student Isaias Zenas, 27, emphasized Messi's broader importance to the nation. He noted, "The last joys we have had as an Argentine people, we owe to him," citing the cups Messi brought during tough economic times.

Messi, who led Argentina to a World Cup and two Copa America titles, concluded his international career with a national record of 125 goals and 68 assists. His final message was simple: "I leave in peace. I gave everything."

headline_marked: [[Dhaka ranks third]] globally in air pollution among 125 major cities
headline: Dhaka ranks third globally in air pollution among 125 major cities
summary: Dhaka's Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 178 this morning, classifying its air as 'unhealthy' according to Swiss-based IQAir. The primary pollutant was PM2.5, nearly 19 times the WHO's annual guideline.
details: Dhaka ranked third globally in air pollution among 125 major cities this morning. According to Swiss-based IQAir, the city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was 178 at 8:30 AM, a level considered 'unhealthy'.

Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and Kolkata, India, held the first and second spots with AQI scores of 213 and 181 respectively. The main pollutant in Dhaka's air was fine particulate matter (PM2.5), with a concentration of 95.5 micrograms per cubic meter, nearly 19 times the World Health Organization's annual guideline.

Beyond Dhaka, Rajshahi recorded the highest pollution among divisional cities with an AQI of 169. Other cities showed significant levels: Khulna 164, Rangpur 157, Mymensingh 155, Barishal 151, Chattogram 142, and Sylhet 112.
Within Dhaka's monitoring centers, Gulshan Lake Park recorded the highest air quality index at 198. Surrounding areas also faced severe pollution, with Gazipur at 220, Savar at 175, and Tongi at 167.
IQAir's index provides real-time data, meaning positions and scores can fluctuate throughout the day. These figures are based on information from 12 monitoring centers in Dhaka.
